goal: Freeze the user's intended Codex-CGKN-Telegram ownership and persistent checkpoint-supervision model as a normative, registered, automatically guarded architecture baseline without claiming the supervisor runtime is already implemented.
acceptance_criteria: A dedicated normative document defines CGKN as the independently running system, Telegram as a CGKN-owned interface, and Codex as the startup/attachment and persistent checkpoint supervisor.

The baseline defines lifecycle, persistent identity, mandatory checkpoints, allowed actions, bounded repair, failure recovery, customer flow, formal-route preservation, conformance criteria, and the current implementation gap.
Request-scoped Codex calls are explicitly transitional or specialist-only and cannot satisfy the persistent-supervision baseline.
AGENTS.md, README, docs/00_kernel_contract.md, and docs/01_contract_registry.md reference the baseline consistently.
Kernel and documentation tests guard the ownership direction, persistent-thread requirement, repair authority, NOT_EVALUATED posture, and unchanged Provider/local_packager route.

quality_metrics.target: all required roles, lifecycle states, checkpoints, actions, failure cases, authority limits, and conformance checks are explicit and internally consistent
quality_metrics.method: document review plus deterministic string/contract guards

quality_metrics.measure: formal generation and delivery route preservation
quality_metrics.target: the baseline retains Provider authorship, formal evidence separation, whiteboard plus agent_session, local_packager, and public_delivery_gate
persistent supervision remains NOT_EVALUATED and the current ephemeral adapter is labeled transitional until runtime evidence exists

prevention: Make ownership direction and prohibited inversion normative before implementing another supervisor adapter.
assurance: Cross-check the baseline against AGENTS.md and the registered Provider/delivery route.
Review automatic repair language for explicit authority and recovery limits.
control: Run JSON validation, document consistency tests, kernel contract tests, and management-pack tests.
improvement: Use this baseline as acceptance input for the next persistent supervisor-host implementation increment.

interface_expectations: Codex starts or attaches to a long-running CGKN service; starting the desktop window alone is not readiness evidence.
CGKN owns Telegram intake and durable project state and emits identity-bound checkpoints.
The supervisor resumes one persistent Codex thread and records process, repository, and checkpoint continuity.
repair_cgkn may change only CGKN-owned artifacts and must retain an auditable diff plus passing proportionate regression before resume.
Provider authorship, formal evidence, local_packager, public_delivery_gate, and delivery authority remain outside Codex supervision.

feedback: The normative baseline now fixes the intended ownership direction, persistent supervision lifecycle, checkpoint and repair model, failure behavior, and unchanged Provider/delivery authority. Documentation and management-contract verification passed. Persistent supervisor runtime implementation remains explicitly NOT_EVALUATED and is not implied by this documentation PASS.

worked: Separating the normative target from the current ephemeral adapter made the architecture correction explicit without falsely claiming implementation.
Registering the baseline in AGENTS.md, the kernel contract, the contract registry, and tests gives future work one enforceable source of runtime ownership truth.
did_not_work: The first management-helper validation passed a directory where the command requires an individual JSON file; validation was rerun correctly for both the management pack and iteration and passed.
experiments: Use the conformance section as the acceptance basis for a separate implementation increment that adds the supervisor host, persistent thread adapter, checkpoint protocol, and repair/restart receipts.
